thesis: Intel completed a $23.0B secondary equity offering on Aug 10-11, selling 210,526,315 shares at $95 with the over-allotment of 31,578,947 shares exercised in full. The stock now trades at $87.47, below that offering price, and the 60-day decline of 33.6% coincides with the supply overhang from that raise rather than any disclosed operating improvement; separate reporting places Intel's CPU market share at a three-decade low. The strongest counter-case is that the raise materially strengthens the balance sheet for the foundry build-out and that the shares still sit well above the 200-day MA of $72.00, but a completed raise of this size is dilution that has already occurred, and buying below the price institutional allocators paid two weeks ago offers no structural edge. This suggests waiting for the overhang to clear rather than entering here.
invalidation: Shares reclaim and hold above the $95 offering price, or Intel discloses a foundry customer win or CPU share stabilisation that reframes the raise as growth funding rather than dilution.

thesis: Semtech reported fiscal Q2 on Aug 25 with EPS of $0.71 against $0.61 consensus and revenue of $341.9M against $328.6M, and guided next-quarter revenue to a $410M midpoint, roughly 14.6% above the $379M analysts expected, with inventory levels improving. Both are already-disclosed company results, not anticipation. The strongest counter-evidence is the pending securities class action alleging management overstated CopperEdge demand over the Nov 2024-Feb 2025 class period — a direct challenge to the credibility of exactly this kind of guidance — but this quarter's beat is a delivered result rather than a forward promise, the related shareholder derivative claims were dismissed in Aug 2026, and Roth Capital raised its target to $190 from $102 on the print. Price of $127.47 sits 21.7% above the 200-day MA of $104.75, so the 60-day drawdown of 18.3% reads as a pullback within an uptrend rather than a break of it. This suggests the disclosed operating trajectory has improved.
invalidation: Q3 revenue lands below the $405M low end of guidance, CopperEdge demand commentary is walked back again, or the securities class action produces a scheduled ruling or adverse finding.
sources: Kessler Topaz (SMTC securities class action): https://www.ktmc.com/semtech-corporation/

thesis: SpaceX reported Q2 on Aug 4 with results above expectations, but capital expenditure rose more than sixfold year over year to $18.37B, of which $15.83B went to AI infrastructure following the February xAI merger, and shares fell 6% after hours. The read is genuinely offsetting: revenue growth and a narrowed net loss on one side, a spending run-rate that pushed last year's loss to $4.9B on the other, with Starlink connectivity still the only profitable segment. The company listed on Jun 12, 2026 at a $161 close, so there is no long price history to judge the trend against, and a separate suit seeking to shut down the gas turbines powering the Colossus 2 data centre puts a $45B Anthropic contract at issue. Phillip Capital has moved to a sell rating with a $75 target. This suggests the beat does not resolve the spending question, and the evidence remains unresolved rather than net-positive.
invalidation: Capital expenditure guidance moderates while connectivity margins hold, or the Colossus 2 turbine litigation resolves without disrupting the Anthropic contract.

thesis: Marvell reports earnings on Aug 27, one day out, which is an unresolved binary event ahead of any plausible next review of this position. The recent company-disclosed item is the Aug 19 commercial agreement granting Alphabet a warrant over roughly 58.97 million shares — about 7% of shares outstanding — at an exercise price of $206.58, which shares upside with the customer at a strike below the current $240.31. The stock has nearly tripled in 2026 and sits about 64% above its 200-day MA of $146.52, so the 13.5% 60-day pullback is a give-back within a very extended advance rather than evidence of deterioration. This suggests no basis for establishing a new position into an earnings print with a fresh equity-linked overhang already disclosed.
invalidation: Aug 27 results and guidance clear expectations and the stock holds its post-print level, at which point the setup can be re-screened without an unresolved binary event in front of it.

thesis: AMD's Q2 (quarter ended Jun 27, reported the first week of August) came in above consensus at $1.66 EPS against $1.62 and $11.55B revenue against $11.28B, with data centre revenue more than doubling. The 11.2% 60-day decline is attributed in reporting to a sector-wide semiconductor sell-off on AI-overspending fears rather than to any disclosed deterioration at AMD, which is a sentiment-driven explanation and limits how much weight the drawdown itself should carry. Real company-specific negatives exist alongside it: a major customer said it would source AI chips from a rival, and the warrants over 320 million shares committed to OpenAI and Meta at $0.01 — close to 20% of the 1.63 billion shares outstanding — will structurally cap reported EPS as milestones vest, though none had vested as of late June and the commitments were disclosed between October 2025 and February 2026. Price of $479.25 sits 44% above the 200-day MA of $332.01. This suggests the disclosed fundamentals remain intact while the pullback is sentiment-led.
invalidation: Data centre revenue growth decelerates on the next print, further major customers move volume to rivals, or warrant vesting milestones are hit in a way that materially resets reported EPS expectations.
